title: Landspace aims to refly recovered Zhuque-3 booster within six months
summary: Landspace, a Chinese commercial launch firm, aims to refly its Zhuque-3 first stage booster within six months after achieving a successful vertical landing on August 18. This milestone marks a significant step in reusable rocket technology for the company.

title: New space transportation policy focuses on increased launch rates
summary: The White House released a new space transportation policy on August 20, aiming to significantly boost the number of launches and reentries. The policy emphasizes increasing launch rates to support the growing space industry.

title: Golden Dome chief touts progress as funding questions loom
summary: The chief of the Golden Dome missile defense program highlights progress while funding concerns persist. The program's leadership, including North Dakota senators, advocates for continued financial support.

title: Elve qualifies millimeter-wave amplifiers for spaceflight
summary: Elve, a California-based startup, has qualified its 100-watt millimeter-wave Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier for spaceflight. The qualification was supported by U.S. Space Force Small Business Innovation Research funding.

title: SpaceWERX selects 11 firms to scale technologies for military space
summary: SpaceWERX has selected 11 companies to receive new STRATFIs for scaling technologies aimed at enhancing military space capabilities. The awardees include Agile Space Industries, Antares Nuclear, EO Solutions, and others.

title: What’s next for ISR in space
summary: A panel of experts discusses the future of Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) in space and its evolving role. The discussion was recorded in May and featured insights from SpaceNews correspondent Debra Werner.

title: Rocket Lab launches 9th satellite for iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab successfully launched its ninth satellite for Japanese radar-imaging company iQPS on August 20. This mission marks another collaboration between Rocket Lab and iQPS in expanding radar satellite constellations.

title: Moog Highlights Huntsville Expansion and New Hardware-in-the-Loop Lab During Space and Missile Defense Symposium
summary: Moog Inc. announced a major expansion of its Huntsville facility, including a new secure Hypersonic/Interceptor Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) lab. The announcement was made during the Space and Missile Defense Symposium.

title: Portal Space Systems to include rideshare payloads on Falcon 9 launch of Supernova
summary: Portal Space Systems has secured a Falcon 9 launch for its first Supernova spacecraft and will provide excess capacity for rideshare payloads. The mission aims to demonstrate the company's technology while accommodating additional payloads.

title: Rock West Composites® Is Premiering Its New STRATOPultrusion™ Product Line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference
summary: Rock West Composites is launching its new STRATOPultrusion™ product line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference. The event will take place in Salt Lake City, Utah, this August.

title: My favorite thing in the night sky appears on Aug. 28 — and it proves Earth is a sphere
summary: A deep partial lunar eclipse on Aug. 28 will reveal Earth's curved shadow moving across the moon, proving its spherical shape. This celestial event offers a striking visual demonstration of Earth's geometry.

title: Could 'dark photons' explain dark matter?
summary: New research proposes that dark matter, composed of 'dark photons,' may not have heated the early universe as previously believed. This challenges existing theories about the nature of dark matter.

title: China's Chang'e 7 moon probe will launch this weekend on the most ambitious lunar mission in history
summary: China is set to launch the Chang'e 7 moon probe on August 24, marking its most ambitious lunar mission to date. The mission will include a lander, rover, hopper, and various science experiments targeting the lunar south pole.

title: SpaceX will try for 1st Starship tower catch 'in a few months,' Elon Musk says
summary: SpaceX plans to attempt the first-ever catch of its Starship upper stage using a launch tower in a few months, with Elon Musk previously suggesting late August as a potential date.

title: Microbes from Earth may survive on the moon, scientists find
summary: Scientists have discovered that microbes from Earth could potentially survive on the moon, suggesting that even disturbances like rover tracks or bootprints might create habitable microenvironments. This finding highlights the resilience of terrestrial life in extreme lunar conditions.

title: 'Wet Hot American Summer': The raunchy 2000s comedy that was actually about a space station falling to Earth
summary: The article reflects on the 2000s comedy 'Wet Hot American Summer,' which humorously depicted a space station falling to Earth. It marks the 25th anniversary of the film's release.

title: A weather satellite 22,000 miles above Earth saved my 2026 total solar eclipse cruise on the Mediterranean Sea
summary: A weather satellite helped ensure a safe and enjoyable total solar eclipse viewing experience for Joe Rao aboard a Mediterranean cruise ship in 2026. The satellite provided critical weather data to navigate the eclipse path.

title: Ludicrous, nonsensical, an affront to canon — 'Strange New Worlds'' puppet episode is an instant classic
summary: Star Trek's collaboration with the Jim Henson Company on a puppet episode of 'Strange New Worlds' has been praised as a hilarious and masterful success despite initial skepticism. The episode is hailed as an instant classic, defying expectations and canon.

title: Mars Express orbiter captures detailed new video of the crater where Mark Watney was stranded in 'The Martian'
summary: Europe's Mars Express orbiter captured a detailed flyover visualization of Schiaparelli Crater on Mars, the location where Mark Watney was stranded in 'The Martian'. The new telemetry-based video showcases the Red Planet's Southern Highlands in high detail.

title: Europe’s Scorching Summer
summary: Europe experienced unprecedented heat waves in 2026, setting new temperature records and causing significant environmental and societal impacts. The extreme weather events highlighted ongoing concerns about climate change and its regional effects.

title: SmallSat 2026
summary: NASA will participate in the SmallSat 2026 event with storytelling sessions by experts and booths at the exhibit hall. The agenda includes presentations on smallsats, supply chain observations, and various NASA missions.

title: Artemis Mission Patches
summary: NASA conducted a terminal countdown simulation for the Artemis III mission at Kennedy Space Center, featuring mission patches from Artemis I and II. The event took place inside the Rocco A. Petrone Launch Control Center.

title: NASA Selects University Teams to Help Advance Aviation Research
summary: NASA selected four university teams to advance aviation research, including supersonic propulsion and urban flight noise reduction. The projects are part of NASA's University Leadership Initiative to support student contributions to real-world flight research.

title: The View from Above: The Gemini Visual Acuity Experiments
summary: NASA astronaut L. Gordon Cooper, Jr. captured 29 color photographs of Earth during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission in May 1963, reporting visibility of vehicles and trains from space.

title: NASA Data Feeds River Forecasts as Snow Drought Effects Linger
summary: NASA Earth science data is being used to enhance machine-learning river forecasts in Washington state, addressing ongoing impacts from a snow drought. These forecasts aid decisions on water management, power generation, and public safety.

title: APOD: 2026 August 20 – The Elephant’s Trunk in Cepheus
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 20, 2026, features an image of the Elephant's Trunk Nebula in the constellation Cepheus. The post includes an explanation of the nebula written by a professional astronomer.

title: An Uncommon Drifter in the Denmark Strait
summary: A massive iceberg was observed in summer 2026, having drifted over 1,000 kilometers south from its likely origin in northeastern Greenland. The unusual drift path was noted in the Denmark Strait.

title: NASA TechLeap Prize: Orbital Clarity Challenge
summary: NASA's TechLeap Prize introduces the Orbital Clarity Challenge to study space weather's impact on Earth's atmosphere and orbital drag. The challenge is a collaboration between NASA's Heliophysics Division, Flight Opportunities program, and Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation.

title: NASA Updates Next Steps for Commercial Swift Boost Mission
summary: NASA and Katalyst Space have postponed the LINK spacecraft's planned capture and boost of a NASA satellite due to an ongoing attitude control issue. The mission will still attempt rendezvous and proximity operations with NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine development for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch around 2026. This positions Stoke Space as a competitor in the reusable launch vehicle market alongside SpaceX's Starship.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket completed its second flight, achieving a successful first-stage landing. This milestone marks progress in reusable rocket technology for the company.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location off the coast of Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 mission following a recent launch failure, while SpaceX's Starlink launches are also scheduled for the same week.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also making progress on its Eclipse mission. The company is promoting its next block of Alpha rockets alongside ongoing development efforts.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual launch pad operations at Cape Canaveral as it restores its primary launch pad at LC-36A. The company aims to enhance its launch capabilities with this expansion.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. The company is expanding its global presence and launch capabilities.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also experiencing a failure. The site launched AI satellites and is preparing for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is advancing the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles. Teams are progressing through various stages of production to prepare for future missions.

title: Launch Preview: Chinese failure opens busy international launch salvo
summary: The week of Aug. 10 featured four international launches across three countries, following a Chinese launch failure. The busy launch schedule highlights a competitive global space industry.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of significant contributions by the European Space Agency.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3, a mission by the European Space Agency (ESA), will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona. The mission is scheduled to launch ahead of the total solar eclipse visible in Europe.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event is part of the mission's testing and observation phase.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to study due to the rarity and brief duration of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to test their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This opportunity allows for direct execution of innovative software in a deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with two satellites, one acting as a coronagraph to block the Sun and observe the solar corona, while the other captures images of the Earth. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona and test precise satellite positioning in space.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together startup companies and the European space industry to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann, a partner at NewSpace Capital, discusses the key technologies shaping the future of space tech. The op-ed highlights emerging innovations that could redefine the industry.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its satellite production capacity and diversify its mission capabilities.

title: Portal Books Dedicated Falcon 9 Amid Constrained Launch Market
summary: Portal Books a dedicated Falcon 9 launch while collaborating with Maverick Space Systems to sell the remaining fairing space for rideshare opportunities in a constrained launch market.

title: SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions: Build, Partner, or Buy?
summary: SpaceX is exploring strategies to compete with major telecom providers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon by expanding into mobile services. The company aims to leverage a multi-billion-dollar revenue opportunity by moving beyond its current direct-to-consumer coverage.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House released its National Security Science & Technology Strategy through the Office of Science and Technology Policy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts in science and technology.

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial nuclear mission to the Moon, partnering with Firefly Aerospace to launch a radioisotope heating unit on a 2028 mission. The demonstration aims to showcase Zeno's capability to provide 5W of power for lunar operations.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The U.S. Space Force's FY27 budget request has been highlighted as a record-breaking $71.3 billion. This budget request has drawn significant attention in the space industry.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered capabilities to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in managing satellite operations more efficiently.

title: HEO Taps Planet Labs to Expand its NEI Network
summary: HEO has partnered with Planet Labs to expand its NEI network to over 50 in-space sensors, enabling more frequent and high-resolution imaging of objects in orbit from multiple angles.

title: DIU, SDA Select Winners for Deorbit-as-a-Service Designs
summary: The Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) selected three companies to design scalable satellite deorbit capabilities, including rendezvous and capture. This initiative aims to address orbital debris mitigation through a 'Deorbit-as-a-Service' approach.
company: Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU)

title: Sypris Electronics Wins Manufacturing Deal to Support LEO Constellation
summary: Sypris Electronics has secured a manufacturing contract to produce power processing units for an unnamed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. The deal marks a significant expansion in the company's involvement in next-generation satellite technology.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C to Build Large-Scale Constellations
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in Series C funding to expand its satellite manufacturing capabilities and build large-scale constellations. The investment will also support the development of differentiated mission capabilities.

title: Phantom Space Names Worth Wray as COO
summary: Phantom Space has appointed Worth Wray as its new Chief Operating Officer (COO) to oversee daily operations, efficiency, and business scaling. The appointment aims to support the company's growth as it increases its operational activities.

title: Rocket Lab Launches SAR Satellite for Japan’s iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab launched a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite for Japan's iQPS from New Zealand on Aug. 21. This marks Rocket Lab's ninth mission for the Japanese SAR company.

title: Rocket Lab’s Bold Move to Acquire Iridium: Analysts Break Down the Strategy
summary: Rocket Lab announced plans to acquire Iridium, marking a significant move in the satellite sector. Analysts are dissecting the strategic implications of this acquisition for both companies.

title: TGS Taps Speedcast for All-LEO Solution
summary: Speedcast has secured a connectivity deal with TGS, implementing an all-LEO solution for its global fleet. TGS is a provider of data and intelligence services.

title: Will Cocos to Lead Vantor’s US Government Business
summary: Vantor has appointed Will Cocos as executive vice president and general manager to lead its U.S. government business, focusing on defense, intelligence, and civil sectors.

title: Katalyst Link Mission is Unable to Rescue NASA Swift Observatory
summary: The Katalyst Link mission, aimed at rescuing NASA's Swift Observatory, has been confirmed unable to complete the rescue. NASA and Katalyst Space confirmed the mission's failure.

title: Kratos Reports Growing Tri-Band Antenna Demand and Debuts New Model
summary: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions has secured multi-million-dollar orders for GAIA antenna systems from international customers. The company also introduced a new model to meet growing tri-band antenna demand.

title: The Rogue Element: How Transnational Cartels Could Establish an Asymmetric Lunar Presence
summary: The Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies warns that the U.S. Space Force must prepare for potential lunar conflict with China. The report highlights concerns about transnational cartels establishing an asymmetric presence on the Moon.
